title: Counterfactual hire tradeoffs and quick recommendation
body:
Purpose: quick scratchpad to compare the candidate we just looped (external senior platform eng), the internal promote option, and a contractor route. Not polished — my notes and heuristics. Meant for fast committee sync and to surface counterfactuals we didn't cover in the loop.

TL;DR:
- Candidate (external) = deep infra pedigree, good latency/kv-cache mental models, strong at kernel/runtime tradeoffs; moderate ramp for our infra conventions.
- Internal promote = lower immediate hiring risk on culture/stack knowledge, but less domain breadth for compiler/kernel work; slower to acquire deep model-serving optimizations.
- Contractor/consultant = fast delivery on targeted tasks (profiling, hotspot fixes), but limited continuity and higher long-term cost. Good as a stopgap.

Candidate quick summary:
- Name: (redacted for public note) — senior runtime/platform engineer, ex-search infra at midsize cloud provider.
- Interview evidence: concrete examples of KV cache eviction strategies, micro-batching heuristics, and a short post-mortem they led for a production latency regression.
- Strengths: latency-first mental model, instrumentation-focused, pragmatic about tradeoffs (quantization vs accuracy), demo'd a small Python harness for kernel experiment.
- Weaknesses / unknowns: limited sustained ownership on multi-region control planes, sparse experience with enterprise compliance (KMS/HSM), communication style can be terse in async docs.

Counterfactual scenarios (cost / time / impact):
1) Hire external candidate (full-time)
   - Ramp: ~8–12 weeks to be independently shipping on runtime perf projects (profiling, kernel selection).
   - Cost: market comp + benefits — ballpark annual OTE ~ $260–320k.
   - Impact: accelerates optimization roadmap, improves observability patterns, could own a rollout for model variant routing.
   - Risk: onboarding overhead around infra conventions (release-engineering, private deploy workflows).

2) Internal promote (senior+ from serving-runtime team)
   - Ramp: ~4–8 weeks to be productive (already knows infra), but may need 12+ months to close gaps in low-level perf/quantization.
   - Cost: lower incremental comp, higher opportunity cost (vacancy in their current role).
   - Impact: smooth cross-team ops, lower people risk, but slower on breakthroughs in kernel/cuda optimizations.

3) Contractor / consulting engagement (3–6 months)
   - Ramp: 1–3 weeks to start delivering scoped work.
   - Cost: hourly premium, overall possibly similar to 6–9 months of full-time comp for high-skill contractors.
   - Impact: tactical wins (profiling hotspots, batching improvements), low long-term ownership -> need to transition knowledge.
   - Risk: continuity and security reviews (esp for private deployments), limited mentorship/ability to improve hiring bench.

Decision framing (what matters to us now):
- Time-to-impact: we need someone who can (a) own a Q2 rollout of model routing fallbacks and (b) reduce token cost via batching/caching suggestions. Time window: 3 months.
- Continuity: ownership across Dedicated and Private products is valuable — avoid churn and knowledge loss.
- Upside vs downside: is this hire likely to push a measurable 10–20% unit-cost reduction within 6 months? Candidate shows the right instincts but unknown delivery velocity here.

Evidence map (what to cite in committee):
- Perf example: candidate described an eviction policy that reduced KV cache churn by ~18% in their previous service (claimed). Asked for data; they forwarded a dashboard screenshot in the follow-up (see linked Slack thread).
- Kernel work: wrote a prototype that swapped GEMM kernel for int8 path in a research repo — good signal for quantization familiarity.
- System ownership: led a 3-person on-call rotation that included incident writeups and RCA.

Risk matrix (likelihood x impact):
- High-likelihood, medium-impact: onboarding friction with release process (medium chance, medium cost).
- Medium-likelihood, high-impact: fails to convert ideas to measurable cost reduction (medium chance, high cost if true).
- Low-likelihood, high-impact: violates security/backdoor risk — mitigated by our hiring screening and SRE review.

Recommendation (quick):
Option A: extend offer at midpoint of band, with a 6-month performance milestone tied to:
  - deliverable A: measurable 10% token-cost reduction on standard test workload OR
  - deliverable B: own rollout for model fallback routing in prod for a single customer segment
Rationale: this balances upside while giving a clear operational gating metric.

Fallback plan: if candidate declines or stalls, offer 3-month contractor engagement to accelerate the two high-impact tasks while running an internal promotion process.

Gating questions for committee (need answers before final vote):
- Can Hiring take-home / engineering exercise be trimmed to a 1-week scoped perf mini-project (so we get signal on delivery)?
- Will comp at mid-band with 6-month milestone be acceptable to EC/recruiting?
- Who from SRE/security needs to do a pre-offer compliance check for contractors coming in on private deployments?

Open unknowns / TODOs (my next steps):
- Follow up with candidate for more telemetry artifacts (full dashboard links) — asked on 3/4, pinged again 3/5.
- Sync with Maya on replacement timeline if we pull from internal promotion pipeline.
- Draft 6-month milestone language for offer letter (short, measurable).
- Confirm contractor vendor list and rough daily rates for 90-day window (ask procurement).

Notes to self (rough heuristics used):
- Prefer internal promote when continuity > need for deep bench expertise; prefer external when we need non-obvious kernel/architectural changes quickly.
- Use contractor only for time-limited, highly scoped profiled tasks; never for long-term ownership.

Slack / links: see linked_artifacts above. Also: Confluence page "perf-runbook-for-routing" (confluence id: CFG-784) is the doc the candidate referenced — worth a read.

Bottom-line personal take: candidate is risky but high upside. I'm leaning to extend with milestone-based offer and contingency contractor support. Want committee's quick read: yes/no/ask for take-home.

-- aria (notes, 3/5)
